meta.title: Python Thinking Partner
meta.description: A study helper for intro Python: guiding questions, a plain-language narration of your own code, and syntax help. No solutions.

breakdown.does: I ask you questions so you can plan in your own words. I won't solve anything.
breakdown.intro: I'll ask you questions; you answer in your own words. I won't solve anything, and there's no place to paste the assignment on purpose.
breakdown.firstQuestion: In your own words, what does the function or program need to do?

narrator.does: I describe what your code literally does, in plain words. I don't judge it or fix it.
narrator.notice: I'll describe what your code does, line by line, in plain words. I won't tell you how to fix it.
narrator.outputHint: Prints and the full error traceback, if there is one.
narrator.outputPlaceholder: Paste the output or the error here
narrator.followUpPlaceholder: e.g. What does line 6 do exactly?
narrator.hypotheticalRefusal: I can only describe the code you submitted, not changed or "what if" versions of it. If you want to see what different code does, edit it yourself and use "Describe different code" to submit the new version.

syntax.does: I explain Python syntax and concepts with small generic examples. I don't write code for your task.
syntax.placeholder: Ask about syntax, a built-in function, or an error message…

recap.buttonHint: Make a NotebookLM video about the concepts from this session
recap.title: Your video recap
recap.intro: Here's a concept summary of today's session (without your code) and a prompt for NotebookLM's video feature.
steps: Open NotebookLM and create a new notebook.
Add a source → choose "Copied text" → paste the recap.
In the Studio panel, choose Video Overview and open its customisation option.
Paste the prompt into the customisation box and generate.
recap.videoPrompt: Create a short, friendly explainer video for a beginner Python student about the concepts in this source. Use simple visual metaphors, walk through each toy example step by step, and keep it under 5 minutes. Do not suggest solutions to any specific assignment.
recap.sharingNote: The recap is concept-only so it's safe to share. Never add your own code to it.

privacy.title: Before you start
privacy.text: Your text is sent to a free AI service and may be used by that provider to improve its models. Don't paste personal information. Nothing is saved here; closing the tab clears everything.

footer.note: Built to follow the course's academic-integrity policy.

rules.title: Rules: how to use this site honestly
rules.intro: Your course allows AI only to help you understand concepts and tools, never to do the work for you. This site is built around that rule.
rules.keyTest: The key test: if an answer could become a direct part of your solution, it's not allowed.
allowed: Understanding error messages, e.g. what `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'` means.
Checking how built-in functions behave, e.g. what `split()` does and returns.
Clarifying language concepts, e.g. the difference between `while` and `for`.
General concepts with simple examples, e.g. "explain recursion".
Syntax questions, e.g. the syntax of a list comprehension.
forbidden: Pasting the assignment and asking AI for a solution.
Asking AI to write a function that does what the assignment requires.
Pasting your code and asking AI to fix it or make it pass the tests.
Using AI-generated code as a starting point and changing it.
Sharing your code with other students in any form (files, screen sharing, a whiteboard, dictating it).
rules.siteTitle: How this site keeps you on the right side
site: There's no place to paste your assignment.
"Break it down" only asks you questions; it never suggests an approach.
"What does my code do?" only describes your code. It doesn't know what the code is supposed to do, so it can't steer you toward a fix.
"Syntax help" explains language features with generic examples (fruits, pets, colours), never code for your task.
The video recap is about concepts only and never contains your code, because sharing code is not allowed.
rules.unsure: If you're unsure whether something is allowed, ask in the course's personal-requests forum.
